rspec: suss: the pack's own name, after the library it reads
RSpec: rspec: the top-level module a group can be opened on, as in RSpec.describe
feature: rspec: the alias of describe that capybara's feature specs use
xdescribe: rspec: opens a group whose examples are skipped
xcontext: rspec: the skipped alias of context
xfeature: rspec: the skipped alias of feature
shared_examples: rspec: defines a group other groups include by name
shared_context: rspec: defines setup other groups include by name
it_behaves_like: rspec: runs a shared group's examples in a nested group titled behaves like and the name
it_should_behave_like: rspec: the same as it_behaves_like, titled it should behave like and the name
include_examples: rspec: runs a shared group's examples in the group it is written in
include_context: rspec: runs a shared context's setup in the group it is written in
scenario: rspec: the alias of it for feature specs
its: rspec-its: declares an example about one attribute of the subject
xit: rspec: declares an example that is skipped
xspecify: rspec: the skipped alias of specify
xexample: rspec: the skipped alias of example
xscenario: rspec: the skipped alias of scenario
skip: rspec: declares a skipped example, skips the running example as a statement, and is the metadata key that skips
pending: rspec: declares a pending example, or marks the running one pending as a statement
before: rspec: a hook whose block runs before each example
prepend_before: rspec: the before hook added to the front of the list
let: rspec: defines a value an example reads by name, run when first read
subject: rspec: defines the group's subject, and reads it inside an example
is_expected: rspec: starts an expectation on the subject
expect: rspec: starts an expectation, and with to receive sets a message expectation
allow: rspec: starts a stub on an object
allow_any_instance_of: rspec: starts a stub on every instance of a class
expect_any_instance_of: rspec: starts a message expectation on every instance of a class
to: rspec: applies a matcher or a stub
not_to: rspec: applies a negated matcher or stub
receive: rspec: the matcher that says which method a stub replaces
receive_messages: rspec: the matcher that stubs several methods at once
have_received: rspec: the matcher that checks a spy was called
stub_const: rspec: replaces a constant for the length of an example
instance_double: rspec: makes a double checked against a class's instance methods
class_double: rspec: makes a double checked against a class's class methods
object_double: rspec: makes a double checked against one object
spy: rspec: makes a double that records every message
instance_spy: rspec: the spy form of instance_double
as_stubbed_const: rspec: makes a class double replace the constant it stands for
described_class: rspec: the class the nearest group around was given
be: rspec: the truthiness and comparison matcher
include: language: Ruby's Module#include, which the adapter reads; RSpec also defines an include matcher, which is what the pack means
match: rspec: the regex and structure matcher
raise_error: rspec: the matcher for a raised error
change: rspec: the matcher for a changed value
an_instance_of: rspec: the argument matcher for an instance of a class
a_kind_of: rspec: the argument matcher for a kind of a class
anything: rspec: the argument matcher that accepts any value
hash_including: rspec: the argument matcher for a hash with some keys
satisfy: rspec: the matcher that runs a block
output: rspec: the matcher for printed output
all: rspec: the matcher that applies another to every element
be_: rspec: the prefix of a predicate matcher, as in be_cancelled
have_: rspec: the prefix of a has_ predicate matcher, as in have_key
